title: Antiferroelectric biased at critical field gives giant differential capacitance
idea: Effect walk: field-induced antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric transition. A ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is held by a built-in work-function bias just below its forward switching field, where dP/dE is 5-10x the linear permittivity, so a +/-0.3 V signal swing moves 5-fF-equivalent charge from a shallow AR~15 cylinder.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1: needs k~70 or AR~115) by borrowing a phase transition's effective k of ~150-300, permitting AR 15-25 pillars with fewer deep-etch steps; sub-loop hysteresis and fatigue are the risks.

title: Inside-out capacitor: block-copolymer pore sponge replaces one tall pillar
idea: Flip the capacitor from a solid pillar into voids: inside each cell footprint a self-assembled block-copolymer template is etched into sacrificial oxide as ~10 nm pores (AR ~20 each), then coated TiN/ZrO2/TiN by ALD, so area comes from many shallow holes instead of one 70:1 pillar.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~2-3x electrode area at one third of the aspect ratio, reaching ~5 fF without AR 115 and removing pillar-collapse yield loss.

title: Magnetoelectric BiFeO3 flips nanomagnets with voltage alone
idea: Shift write energy to the atto-joule scale: a voltage across thin BiFeO3 rotates its antiferromagnetic order, which exchange-couples to a CoFe free layer, writing a magnet with no current and reading it by TMR.
why: Voltage floor and energy: ~100 mV, aJ writes break the CV2 wall; no capacitor and no refresh.

title: Sticky note: stiction itself becomes the bit in fluorine-free NEMS
idea: Stimulus 'sticky note' (sticks, peels, re-sticks) -> a TiN nano-cantilever is either stuck to its pad by van der Waals adhesion (1) or freed by a thermal-bimorph or repulsive electrostatic kick (0), read by contact current. MEMS normally fights stiction with fluorinated anti-stiction monolayers and releases with HF vapor or XeF2; here an amorphous-carbon sacrificial layer is ashed in O2 and stiction is the feature.
why: Zero-power nonvolatile mechanical bit with no leakage (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1), stackable in BEOL (fact 2); no fluorinated release or coating chemistry.

title: Light-latched bits: self-electro-optic effect device memory planes
idea: Reverse light's role from signal to holder: arrays of symmetric SEEDs (GaAs quantum-well p-i-n pairs, 1990s Bell Labs, ~5 um pixels) latch a bit through photocurrent feedback under a uniform bias beam; pages are written and read by light in parallel with no electrical wires.
why: Data movement (fact 5): page-parallel optical I/O at fJ/bit and static retention while illuminated; low density (~25 um2/bit) fits optically linked buffers, not bulk capacity.

title: Drum optimum-programming compiler for in-flight delay-line memories
idea: 1950s drum programmers (SOAP for the IBM 650) placed each word where it would pass under the head just in time. Build a compiler and runtime that schedules AI tensor tiles into recirculating loops (acoustic, photonic, spin-wave) so each tile reaches its tap exactly when the accelerator needs it.
why: Turns circulation delay into near-zero effective latency for predictable AI dataflows (weights, KV streams), so cheap delay storage displaces DRAM capacity with no fab at all.

title: Mn: rare-earth-free τ-MnAl nanomagnets run deliberately volatile like DRAM
idea: Build perpendicular MTJ free layers from tau-phase MnAl (Mn and Al only, no Co, Pt or rare earths) sized for thermal stability ~25 instead of ~60, giving seconds-to-minutes retention with ~1% thermal flips between scrubs; write current drops ~2-3x and the cell shrinks.
why: Volatile MRAM as a DRAM replacement with unlimited endurance, non-destructive read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1); tolerating 1% flips is what lets stability, write energy and size fall.

title: Vortex nanoring core memory threaded by word and bit lines
idea: IFR: core memory's unlimited endurance at nanoscale. Closest achievable: permalloy nanorings threaded by a vertical via hold clockwise or counter-clockwise vortex chirality, set by coincident current in the via and a bitline as in 1950s cores, and read by a small TMR stack on the ring.
why: Nonvolatile, unlimited endurance, closed flux means no stray field (row-hammer immune, fact 9) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Bell Labs 1952 ferroelectric matrix revived with square-loop HZO superlattices
idea: The first ferroelectric memories (BaTiO3 crystal matrices, 1952) were transistor-free passive crosspoints that died of half-select disturb because their loops were not square. Revive the passive matrix with nucleation-limited HfZrO/ZrO2 superlattices whose Al2O3 pinning planes make switching probability at V/3 <1e-12 per pulse while full V switches in 10 ns, stacking 8 passive decks in BEOL.
why: No access device and 8 decks give ~4F2/8 effective cell, ~5-10x bits per mask (Facts 2, 4); non-volatile so no refresh (Fact 3); still destructive read with write-back.

title: Williams-tube revival: field-emitter arrays write charge spots on dielectric
idea: The 1940s Williams tube stored bits as charge spots on a CRT face. Its nanoscale successor is a vacuum-sealed array of Spindt field-emission tips, each deflecting its beam over an 8x8 field of spots to write and read electron charge in a trap-rich dielectric film. The bit lives in the film, with no access transistor.
why: Facts 3 and 4: the storage medium is an unpatterned film, so no transistor or litho-defined capacitor is needed per cell. Vacuum-isolated traps cut refresh, and the cost moves into emitter arrays.

title: WDM optical readout of quantum-dot charge storage cells
idea: Fuse silicon-photonic wavelength multiplexing with charge storage: each cell is a quantum dot coupled to a micro-ring whose resonance shifts through the quantum-confined Stark effect when the dot holds charge. One waveguide carrying 64 wavelengths reads 64 cells at once, non-destructively, with no bitline or sense amp.
why: Facts 5, 7, 8: no destructive read or page overfetch, data leaves the array as light at ~0.1-0.5 pJ/bit, and the sense-amp periphery shrinks.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly carving sub-10 nm storage islands without EUV
idea: Anneal a high-chi block copolymer (e.g., PS-b-PDMS) at <=250 C so it self-assembles into hexagonal 8-10 nm-pitch dots registered to a coarse DUV guide pattern. Transfer the dots as hard masks that define magnetic, ferroic or charge-storage islands; pitch comes from chi*N thermodynamics, not photon wavelength.
why: Sub-10 nm bit definition with no EUV (fact 4), raising density for many BEOL storage elements.

title: Four-level analog charge storage borrowed from particle-detector pipelines
idea: Collider front-ends store analog samples on capacitors at 40 MHz; applied to DRAM, each cell holds one of four voltage levels, sensed by a two-step successive-approximation sense amplifier, with a per-row reference cell written alongside the data to track leakage drift. Two bits live in one capacitor.
why: 2x bits per capacitor (density, ~40% lower cost per bit) on existing cells; needs ~3x tighter signal margins and faster refresh, so it pairs with larger-Cs or lower-leakage cells.

title: Dye-bath ferrocene grafting: quantized multi-level molecular charge storage
idea: Copy textile mordant dyeing: dip the wafer so the cup walls graft a mixed monolayer of ferrocene and biferrocene derivatives (Fe, C, H). Their distinct redox potentials store charge in discrete plateaus (2 bits per cell), and leakage cannot drift a level until a whole plateau has emptied.
why: Fact 3: quantized levels tolerate the leakage tail, allowing ~10x longer refresh intervals and 2 bits per cell. Iron-based chemistry needs no scarce metals.

title: Diffusion-barrier monolayer at storage-node contact for 200C retention
idea: Downhole tools at 200C expose tail cells whose mid-gap traps come from contact-metal atoms diffusing into the storage junction; an ALD AlN or hBN monolayer is deposited blanket into the existing storage-node contact holes as a diffusion barrier, and the single added mask only strips it from periphery contacts. The storage junction stays defect-free so its generation current collapses.
why: Trims the leakage tail (fact 3) by ~10x, stretching refresh interval and saving 10-20% of idle power; added contact resistance must stay below ~10 kohm.

title: Strain-coupled piezo layer flipping a magnetostrictive nanomagnet
idea: Combine a thin AlScN piezoelectric pad with an elliptical magnetostrictive FeGa nanomagnet on top: a voltage pulse strains the magnet and rotates its easy axis by 90 degrees, and a timed pulse pair completes a 180-degree flip. A tunnel junction stacked above reads the state; writing draws almost no current, and the magnet holds the bit indefinitely.
why: Zero refresh, ~1 aJ writes (about 100x below STT-MRAM), effectively unlimited magnetic endurance; AlScN is CMOS-compatible.

title: Mechanical access: NEMS relay air gap isolates every cell
idea: Swap electronic isolation for a physical gap: each capacitor reaches its bitline through a nanoscale electrostatic TiN or carbon cantilever relay (5 nm gap) that closes only when the wordline pulls it; open, the leakage is literally zero, and the relay needs no doped silicon so it builds in the BEOL.
why: Leakage tail and 3D (facts 2,3): retention set only by the capacitor dielectric (hours) and BEOL-stackable cells; risk is contact wear capping endurance near 1e10-1e12.

title: Hybrid gain cell: silicon read transistor, WSe2 write transistor
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): ACT/RD/WR/PRE behavior unchanged. A 2T gain cell stores the bit on the gate of a Si FinFET read device, written through a BEOL monolayer WSe2 p-FET whose 1.6 eV gap and atomically thin body give off current below 1e-19 A; reads are nondestructive, so the die skips restore inside tRAS and uses the slack to precharge early.
why: No capacitor (facts 1, 2), minutes of retention (fact 3), and no restore energy for the 128x overfetched page (fact 8); 2D transfer yield is the risk.

title: Po: memory made of seawater — track-etched nanofluidic iontronic membrane
idea: Po: memory made of seawater. Extracted: fill ion-track-etched polymer membranes (mass-produced for filtration, ~1e9 conical ~10 nm channels/cm2) with aqueous salt; each asymmetric nanochannel accumulates or depletes ions under a pulse (concentration polarization) and holds a hysteretic conductance state between printed face electrodes.
why: Polymer, water and salt avoid helium, tungsten and quartz chokepoints on R2R lines, aiming at a 100x+ cost cut. Trade-offs: seconds-scale volatility, us-ms speed, sealing against evaporation.

title: Na: big-capacitor LTPS DRAM on soda-lime glass in idle LCD fabs
idea: Build 1T1C DRAM with low-temperature poly-Si transistors and large planar capacitors on soda-lime glass (SiN barrier against Na+) in depreciated Gen-6/8 LCD lines at 1-2 um rules; a 2.8 m2 Gen-6 panel holds ~1e11 cells (~10 GB after periphery), and panel defect densities that would kill logic are fine because <=1% bad cells are mapped and coded out.
why: Uses already-paid-for display capital instead of $15B fabs (capital intensity) with no high-AR etch (fact 1) and no EUV (fact 4); a bulk-capacity tier for AI servers.

title: Microring resonance reads capacitor charge nondestructively
idea: Scale shift into photonics: the storage node is a pn junction embedded in a silicon microring; stored charge shifts the ring resonance by plasma dispersion, so a WDM probe beam reads hundreds of bits per waveguide without discharging them.
why: Destructive read and data movement: removes sense-amp restore and lets reads leave the die optically, ~1 pJ/bit target.

title: Al: AlN acoustic delay loop recirculates bits as phonons
idea: Launch bits as 10 GHz acoustic pulses into a folded AlN/Al2O3 acoustic waveguide where sound travels ~10 km/s, so a 1 mm loop holds ~1,000 bits for 100 ns; a piezo transducer reads and rewrites each bit per pass, and soft-decision regeneration absorbs ~1% raw symbol errors from dispersion and noise.
why: A capacitor-free, transistor-light storage element of Al, N and O; sound is ~30,000x slower than light, so bits pack ~30,000x tighter than an optical loop, which suits streaming KV-cache traffic (fact 5).

title: Triple-barrier resonant-tunneling III-V charge node on GaAs substrates
idea: Invert 'a retention barrier must be thick so writes need high voltage' -> make it thick but resonantly transparent at one voltage. An InAs/AlSb triple-barrier stack on GaAs or InP lets electrons enter an InAs storage well only when ~2.5 V aligns quantized levels, while the ~2.1 eV AlSb offset holds charge for years at zero bias.
why: Non-volatile charge with ~100x lower write energy than flash and high endurance (no oxide trap generation), usable as refresh-free DRAM (facts 3, 10) on U.S. III-V RF/optoelectronic lines; builds on ULTRARAM-type prior art.

title: Check-valve bottling: resonant-tunnel barrier seals a quantum-well charge
idea: Like a bottle with a one-way valve cap, an InAs quantum well holds charge behind an InAs/AlSb triple barrier. The barrier is opaque at rest (~2.1 eV AlSb offset) and turns resonantly transparent only near 2.5 V, filling or emptying the well in ns.
why: Fact 3: retention of hours to years nearly removes refresh while writes stay fast and low-energy. It also gives U.S. III-V fabs a memory product.

title: Neon-lamp bistability via broken-gap 2D Esaki diode latch
idea: Early computers latched bits in neon lamps' negative resistance; build a cell where two series broken-gap tunnel diodes (e.g., black phosphorus/SnSe2 or WSe2/SnSe2) form a Goto-pair bistable node with pA valley current, plus one access transistor, so the node self-restores like SRAM in ~3F2 with no refresh.
why: Fact 3 and SRAM density: static, refresh-free storage with standby current 100-1000x below SRAM; III-V tunneling SRAM failed on peak-to-valley ratio, so the bet is 2D broken-gap junctions with PVR>10 at room temperature.

title: CuInP2S6 quadruple-well ferroelectric stores two bits per cell on mica
idea: Invert 'a ferroelectric gives two states' -> use one with four. Layered CuInP2S6 has a quadruple-well potential (low and high polarization of each sign set by Cu displacement), grown by van der Waals epitaxy on cleavable mica and read through the threshold shift of a 2D-semiconductor channel.
why: 2 bits per cell with non-destructive FET read and trap-free vdW interfaces, on a non-silicon flexible substrate; Cu migration endurance and the ~315 K Curie point are the risks.

title: Piezo-latched snap-through nanobeam holds bits as mechanical buckling
idea: Effect walk: piezoelectricity + Euler buckling. A 200-nm AlN/Si bimorph beam is built pre-compressed so it rests in one of two buckled states (up or down); a +/-1 V piezo pulse snaps it through in ~ns, and a monolayer MoS2 strain gauge at the beam root reads the state non-destructively by piezoresistance.
why: The bit sits behind an elastic energy barrier (>100 kT), not a charge, so there is no leakage tail or refresh (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1) and no row-hammer coupling (fact 9); beams stack in BEOL without EUV, though pitch is ~4-8F per layer.

title: Pre-buckled 2D membrane snap-through as a leak-free mechanical bit
idea: Clamp a 20 nm MoS2 or graphene drum under compressive prestrain so it has two buckled states separated by an elastic barrier of ~1 eV (~40 kT). A ~1 V electrostatic pulse snaps it through in ~1/f0 ~ 1 ns, and a local sense transistor reads up/down as a ~10 aF capacitance change.
why: A mechanical position has no leakage path, so retention is set by the elastic barrier, not a 13 fA tail, and refresh (fact 3) disappears. There is no storage capacitor (fact 1), and write energy is ~CV2 ~ 10 aJ.

title: Leakage-twinned differential cell where drain currents cancel
idea: Worsen: let each capacitor leak through its own random tail transistor. Flip: store the bit as the charge difference between two half-size capacitors sharing one split-fin access device and one junction, so the dominant leakage (GIDL, junction trap-assisted tunneling) drains both equally and the differential signal survives ~10x longer.
why: Attacks the retention tail (fact 3): refresh interval 5-10x longer; half-size caps offset the 2C area penalty.

title: Charge-order ferroelectric switches by electron hopping, not ion motion
idea: Effect walk: electronic ferroelectricity from charge ordering. Use a mixed-valence oxide (LuFe2O4-type, or a rare-earth-free charge-ordered ferrite or manganite) whose polarization comes from Fe2+/Fe3+ ordering, so switching moves electrons between sites rather than displacing ions, at ~meV per unit cell with no oxygen-vacancy fatigue.
why: Electron-only switching promises ~10x lower switching charge-voltage product and fatigue-free endurance for a polar storage cell; room-temperature electronic ferroelectricity in these materials is contested.

title: Swap layer-by-layer 3D stacking for rolling one patterned membrane
idea: Pattern one planar layer of thin-film gain cells with DUV on a strained SiNx bilayer, release it, and let the built-in strain roll it into a 20-winding tube. Each winding becomes a memory tier, and the tiers connect through edge contacts along the roll axis.
why: Gives 20 tiers from one deposition and patterning sequence (fact 2), so cost does not grow with the tier count, and no EUV is used (fact 4).

title: Po: memory is a record player — probe-array ferroelectric domain film
idea: Po: memory is a record player. Extracted: a 10,000-tip MEMS cantilever array scans a blanket LiNbO3 or PZT thin film, writing ~10 nm polarization domains with tip voltage and reading them non-destructively by piezoresponse, so the medium is unpatterned and only the tips need lithography.
why: A blanket film at Tb/in2 density is >100x cheaper per GB than DRAM. Trade-offs: us-ms access, tip wear, shock sensitivity.

title: Diatom silaffin chemistry: liquid-phase high-k grown inside deep pores
idea: Diatoms grow nanostructured silica at room temperature from dilute silicic acid using silaffin peptides and polyamines. Coat the capacitor holes with a polyamine monolayer that catalyses local hydrolysis of Ti/Zr/Nb alkoxides from solution. This builds a conformal 4-5 nm high-k layer that stops growing once it buries the catalyst, deep inside AR >100 pores and without vacuum ALD.
why: Capital and AR (facts 1, 4): conformal dielectric at AR >100, where ALD purge times explode, on liquid tools costing ~1/5 of an ALD cluster. It also opens Nb2O5/TiO2 (k 40-80).

title: Gen-10.5 display fabs print 1T1C memory panels
idea: Scale up from wafer to 3 m glass: every LCD pixel is already a TFT plus storage capacitor, so retool display fabs to print oxide-TFT 1T1C arrays at ~1 um rules across whole panels, diced into far-memory tiles.
why: Capital intensity and US manufacturability: panel cost ~$100-300/m2 makes a slower capacity tier at single-digit $/GB with no EUV and no Spruce Pine crucibles.

title: Chromatophore stretch-read: MEMS capacitor plate pulled away before sensing
idea: Cephalopod chromatophores change size because muscles stretch a pigment sac. Here the storage capacitor's top plate is a nanomembrane, and just before read an actuation electrode pulls it away from the node. With charge Q fixed, cutting C by 5x raises the node voltage 5x (V=Q/C), so a tiny low-AR capacitor gives a full-size sense signal.
why: Charge wall and AR (facts 1, 4): a ~1 fF near-planar cell could deliver the signal of a 5 fF pillar, with no AR 60-75 etch. A 50 nm membrane switches in ~10 ns.

title: Plywood veneer slicing: film-thickness-defined 5-nm electrode combs
idea: Veneer exposes the edges of thin layers: grow 40 alternating 5-nm ALD TiN/Al2O3 layers on a sidewall (or MBE GaAs/AlGaAs, then cleave) and use the exposed edge as a stamp or mask (SNAP-style) to transfer a 10-nm-pitch line array; cross two such arrays with ultrathin ZrO2 so each intersection is a storage capacitor for gain-cell or diode-isolated arrays.
why: Fact 4: 10-nm-pitch lines defined by film thickness rather than lithography, beyond EUV resolution with an ALD tool; fits a university fab; line fan-out contacts and crossbar sneak paths are the risks.

title: Crowe-cell persistent-current loops with nanocryotron readout for cryogenic AI
idea: The 1957 Crowe cell stored bits as clockwise or counter-clockwise supercurrent in a thin-film loop. Build it from 100-nm NbN kinetic-inductance loops read by the nTron (the modern three-terminal cryotron), stacked with cryo-CMOS or SFQ accelerators in dedicated AI pods.
why: Zero static dissipation, zero refresh, ~1e-19 J switching (Facts 3, 10); only pays at pod scale after ~400 W/W 4 K cooling overhead; target 10x system energy per bit including cooling.

title: MoO2-templated rutile TiO2 capacitor: k of 90 without ruthenium
idea: Box = {medium: charge in rutile-phase TiO2 (k~80-100) | access: Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C pillar at AR ~30:1 | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: ALD from TiCl4 made in the U.S. from Florida/Georgia ilmenite, on a rutile-structured MoO2 bottom electrode from Colorado molybdenum}. MoO2 shares the rutile lattice, so it templates rutile TiO2 at low temperature the way RuO2 does, and light Al doping holds leakage down.
why: Fact 1 calls for k~70: this delivers it with domestic elements, removes Ru (South Africa) from the stack and cuts AR ~2x.

title: Goto parametron revived as phase-bistable NEMS resonator bits
idea: Goto's 1954 parametron stored a bit as the 0 or pi phase of an oscillator pumped at twice its frequency. Use arrays of ~1 GHz AlScN or SiN NEMS beams pumped by a shared 2 GHz line; a bit is the vibration phase, written by a small seed pulse, read by phase-sensitive piezo detection, and majority-voted in place.
why: Holding set by mechanical Q, not junction leakage, so no leakage tail (Fact 3); a shared pump replaces per-row refresh; in-place majority logic trims data movement (Fact 5); needs <1 fW pump per bit.

title: Endohedral ion-in-cage dipole: one molecule, one bit
idea: Scarcity rule: the bit gets one molecule of space. A metal ion inside an elongated fullerene or nitride-cluster cage (Li+@C70-type) sits in one of two off-center wells, a gate field flips it, and the dipole shifts the threshold of an underlying 2D transistor. No bond breaks, and the cage is chosen for a ~0.8 eV barrier giving ms-s retention.
why: Self-assembled monolayer density near 1 nm2 per bit bypasses the litho wall (fact 4) with attojoule writes and unbounded cycling; barrier engineering and single-molecule readout are speculative.

title: Coaxial capacitor shell wraps the vertical access transistor
idea: Collapse two scales into one pillar: the vertical channel transistor sits in the core and the storage capacitor is a coaxial dielectric/electrode shell wrapped around its upper half, so a 4F2 footprint holds both.
why: Density: 6F2 to 4F2 (~33% area gain) without separate capacitor landing pads.

title: Liquid-nitrogen planar DRAM: helium-free cold shrinks the capacitor tenfold
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a planar 0.5 fF ZrO2 MIM with no pillar | access: Si FET at 77 K | sense: low-noise cryogenic SA | integration: memory sleds immersed in LN2 from U.S. air-separation plants | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: relaxed-pitch patterning with a U.S. multibeam e-beam writer}. At 77 K subthreshold and junction leakage drop by more than 1e6, so retention reaches minutes even with a tiny planar capacitor, and nitrogen cooling avoids the helium chokepoint entirely.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: no high-AR capacitor, essentially no refresh, no EUV; LN2 is cheap and made domestically.

title: Statolith shuttle: nanoparticle moves between two ends of a sealed cavity
idea: Plant-root statoliths are dense starch grains that settle inside cells to record orientation. Seal a 10 nm conductive nanoparticle (Ru or a carbon onion) in a 30 nm vacuum nanocavity with an electrode at each end. An electrostatic pulse moves it to one end, where van der Waals adhesion holds it, and the bit is read by capacitance or tunnel current at that end.
why: Non-volatile with no bond breaking and so no material wear; ~1 ns transit over 20 nm and unlimited endurance in principle. Uses CMOS-compatible sealed air-gap processes.

title: Bamboo-node grow-up pillar capacitors with periodic diaphragms
idea: Bamboo reaches extreme slenderness by growing upward with a nodal diaphragm every few diameters. Grow the storage-node pillars bottom-up by area-selective TiN deposition through a sacrificial oxide stack, and add a thin SiN diaphragm lattice every ~150 nm of height. AR >150 pillars then neither lean nor stick, and nothing has to be etched at that AR.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): AR 115-150 gives Cs ~8-10 fF without a new high-k. It bypasses etch AR limits and pillar leaning, and uses cheap repeated deposition rather than EUV.

title: Printed relaxor terpolymer dielectric reaching k of 50
idea: IFR: a printable dielectric with ceramic-class permittivity. Closest achievable: slot-die coat P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) relaxor terpolymer (k ~50 at room temperature, slim hysteresis) as the storage-capacitor dielectric, optionally loaded with BaTiO3 nanocubes to push higher.
why: Fact 1: approaches the k~70 target in a printable low-temperature film at cents per area.

title: Anodic rutile TiO2 dielectric grown like electrolytic capacitors
idea: Combine electrolytic-capacitor anodization with DRAM: line the capacitor hole with Ti and anodize it in a non-aqueous electrolyte, growing a conformal, self-limiting oxide whose thickness is set by voltage, on a rutile SnO2 template so it crystallizes as rutile TiO2 (k~80-100). Electrochemistry coats any aspect ratio without ALD, and weak spots self-heal because current crowds there and grows more oxide.
why: Fact 1 and capital: k~80 meets the k~70 target; wet electrochemical cells replace several ALD chambers; self-healing trims the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric FeFET built from U.S. borax and aluminum
idea: Box = {medium: wurtzite AlBN polarization | access: Si FET whose gate dielectric is the AlBN film | sense: nondestructive threshold shift | integration: BEOL plus an SRAM write-coalescing buffer that keeps each cell below 1e9 cycles in 10 years | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: reactive sputtering with boron from Boron, California}. AlBN switches like AlScN but needs no scandium (imported), so every element in the stack (Al, B, N, Si, Mo) is mined and refined in the U.S.
why: Scarce-resource intensity and U.S. manufacturability: nonvolatile and refresh-free with a fully domestic element list; the architecture covers the endurance gap.

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor parked at its field-induced transition knee
idea: Invert 'the capacitor dielectric operates linearly around zero bias' -> park it on a phase transition. A ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is DC-biased by the plate line to the edge of its AFE-to-FE transition, where dP/dE (effective k) is 5-10x the linear value, and data is stored as a small +/- swing around that knee.
why: Recovers the k~70 regime fact 1 demands, so ~5 fF fits at AR ~20-30 instead of 60-75 using existing HfZrO ALD; risks are hysteresis loss, temperature drift of the knee and fatigue.

title: Po: the bit is a chemical reaction — polyoxometalate quantized-charge node
idea: Po: the bit is a chemical reaction. Extracted: a monolayer of polyoxometalate clusters on the storage electrode accepts 1, 2, 3 or 4 electrons at discrete, well-separated redox potentials, so each node stores 2 bits as quantized molecular charge states instead of a fragile analog voltage.
why: 2 bits per cell with built-in level separation and redox capacitance instead of tall pillars (facts 1, 4). Thermal stability of the molecules through BEOL is the risk.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor with Helmholtz-scale gap
idea: MAGNIFY areal capacitance ~100x with an electric double layer: a 3-nm solid proton conductor (hydrated ZrO2 or phosphosilicate glass) between blocking electrodes stores charge in a ~0.5-nm Helmholtz layer (~10-20 uF/cm2), so a planar 20x20 nm node reaches ~0.08 fF, enough for a gain-cell read gate with no high-AR etch.
why: Removes the capacitor etch (fact 1, fact 4 capital); ionic relaxation at nm thickness must reach < 100 ns.

title: Read by emptying with a spoon: charge-metering multilevel readout
idea: Reverse sensing from measuring a level to counting scoops: a ~100 fF 180 nm cell stores one of 16 charge levels; readout clocks the charge through a CCD-style metering gate that skims fixed ~6 fC packets onto the bitline while a counter tallies packets until empty, a 4-bit value without an analog ADC.
why: Density at relaxed litho (fact 4): 4 bits/cell cuts the ~225x area penalty of 180 nm to ~56x before tiering, on depreciated tools; risk is metering accuracy and ~16-clock read time.

title: Ionic-liquid nanopore double-layer cell stores charge at angstrom separation
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics (liquid replaces solid): fill a sealed ~20-nm blocking-electrode pore per cell with a high-conductivity ionic liquid whose electric double layer (~0.5-nm Helmholtz gap) gives 10-20 uF/cm2 at under 1 V, versus ~8 uF/cm2 for best solid high-k. Contradiction resolved: more charge vs. lower voltage.
why: Facts 1 and 10: ~2x charge per area at sub-1 V; charging RC estimated 30-300 ns in a pore, so speed and self-discharge are the open risks.

title: Kitchen sponge: electrodeposited MnO2 pseudocapacitive storage node
idea: Stimulus 'kitchen sponge' (soaks up far more than its surface suggests) -> coat the storage node with ~3 nm MnO2 grown by aqueous electrodeposition from a manganese sulfate bath, with a thin hydrated ZrO2 proton conductor as solid electrolyte; surface Mn3+/Mn4+ redox stores ~10-50x the charge of a dielectric of equal area.
why: A planar ~30 nm^2 pad stores ~5 fF-equivalent charge, replacing 70:1 pillars (fact 1) and deep etch/EUV (fact 4); abundant Mn, fluorine-free aqueous bath.

title: Electroplated pseudocapacitor bit: hydrous RuO2 stores charge as surface protons
idea: Use electroplating to fill each shallow cup with hydrous RuO2.xH2O. Charge is held by fast surface proton redox (pseudocapacitance) rather than a dielectric, ~10-50x a dielectric capacitor per real area. A thin solid proton conductor is the separator.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF from a cup of AR ~5-10, so no deep capacitor etch. The main risk is whether the redox kinetics reach ns.

title: Swap lithography for thermal fiber drawing of capacitor preforms
idea: Build a cm-scale preform of coaxial metal/glass capacitors and thermally draw it 10^4x into fibers with sub-50-nm features. Stack and redraw the fibers into an ordered bundle (as in fiber-optic faceplates), then slice it into capacitor wafers bonded onto DUV access-transistor arrays with oversized landing pads.
why: Makes nanoscale storage capacitors with no lithography at all (fact 4), at drawing rates of km per hour, using furnaces instead of fabs (capital axis).

title: Single-electron transistor sensing attofarad storage nodes
idea: Combine a room-temperature silicon single-electron transistor (sub-3 nm island) as the in-cell sense element with a 10-50 aF storage node, so a few hundred electrons, not ~30,000, encode a bit. The SET's Coulomb oscillations turn each few-electron change into a large current change, read through a gain path that never discharges the node.
why: Facts 1 and 10: the capacitor shrinks ~100x (no high-AR pillars) and storage swings can drop to ~0.3 V; write energy falls ~10x.

title: UV-transparent lid lets depots erase trapped charge in oxide storage layers
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution (optical for electrical): for back-end oxide-semiconductor storage tiers that sit at the top of the stack, package them under a fused-silica window like an EPROM; in a repair depot, deep-UV de-traps charge accumulated in the gate dielectric and channel, restoring threshold voltage and retention without electrical stress.
why: Fact 3 drift reversal and module reuse; turns threshold-voltage drift from a scrap cause into a serviceable condition.

title: Jelly-roll memory: roll a display-fab sheet into dense cylinders
idea: Adapt cylindrical Li-ion jelly rolls: fabricate a large thin oxide-TFT gain-cell array on a strained release layer at display-fab cost per area, then self-roll it into 100-winding micro-cylinders whose edge lines contact a CMOS base die.
why: 10x at same cost: display fabs make area ~100x cheaper per m2 than DRAM wafers, so 100 windings of a 1/10-density sheet give ~10x bits per footprint at equal cost.

title: Display-fab DRAM panels: magnify area, minify cost per area
idea: MAGNIFY substrate area ~1000x and MINIFY cost per m2: a 10-person team designs 1T1C arrays of oxide or LTPS TFTs at ~3 um pitch and buys Gen-8.5 glass runs from idle LCD fabs; a 5.5 m2 sheet of ~10 um2 cells holds ~70 GB raw, diced into slabs bonded to logic by panel-level fan-out.
why: Zero EUV and uses depreciated display capital (fact 4), ally-sourced capacity; at ~$10-20/GB it serves a slower 100-ns tier, not the hottest DRAM.

title: Swap capacitor electrons for flux quantum in kinetic-inductance nanowire loop
idea: At 4 K, a NbN or NbTiN nanowire loop whose kinetic inductance is ~100x its geometric inductance stores one flux quantum in under 1 um2. It is written and read by nanocryotron (nTron) gates instead of large Josephson junctions.
why: Zero static power, ~aJ writes and no refresh for superconducting and quantum processors, which then need no room-temperature DRAM; ~10x denser than SFQ memory built on geometric inductance.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops from astronomy photon detectors
idea: Borrow MKID detectors and MRI persistent switches: store the bit as a persistent current in a 100 nm NbN nanowire loop whose large kinetic inductance lets the loop be tiny, switched by a nanowire heater-cryotron, for cryogenic AI racks.
why: Energy per bit (attojoule writes, zero refresh) and density in cryogenic systems; uses no EUV, no capacitor and no tungsten.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loop storing a single flux quantum
idea: MINIFY the superconducting memory loop from ~10 um2 to ~0.1 um2 by replacing geometric inductance with NbN nanowire kinetic inductance; a bit is one circulating fluxon, written and read by nanocryotron (nTron) gates at 4 K.
why: Zero static power, ps access, unlimited endurance for cryogenic AI and quantum controllers, with density approaching DRAM at 4 K (facts 3, 5).

title: Europa alien: kinetic-inductance nanowire persistent-current loop
idea: An alien from icy Europa assumes memory lives in the cold. A superconducting NbN nanowire loop holds a persistent current, clockwise or counter-clockwise, as a trapped flux quantum. Kinetic inductance lets the loop shrink to ~100 nm, and a nanocryotron reads it.
why: Zero leakage and femtojoule switching for cryogenic AI and quantum datacenters (facts 3, 5, 10).

title: Volatile flash: ultrathin-tunnel charge-trap cells built on 3D-NAND lines
idea: Box = {medium: electrons in a SiN trap layer behind a 1.2 nm direct-tunneling oxide | access: the storage FET itself, NOR-wired | sense: nondestructive threshold read | integration: 200-layer vertical string rewired as NOR | substrate: Si | fab: unchanged 3D-NAND tool set}. Thinning the tunnel oxide trades 10-year retention for ~1-10 s and lets 4-5 V direct-tunneling writes finish in ~10 ns without the Fowler-Nordheim stress that wears out flash, with refresh every second instead of every 64 ms.
why: Facts 2, 3, 4: turns idle, depreciated 3D-NAND capacity into 3D DRAM-class memory with 15x less refresh and 200+ layer density.

title: Avalanche-multiplying read transistor amplifies sub-femtofarad nodes
idea: MAGNIFY read signal 50-100x: the gain-cell read device is an impact-ionization MOS (I-MOS) biased just below breakdown only during read, so ~0.05 fF of stored gate charge switches avalanche on or off with a sub-5 mV/decade slope.
why: Lets Cs shrink ~50x (fact 1) and cuts read energy; hot-carrier wear is bounded because the avalanche bias is applied ~1e-9 of the time.

title: Antiferroelectric-biased capacitor rides the steep switching slope
idea: MAGNIFY dQ/dV: a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is pre-biased by the plate to just below its AFE-to-FE field, so the 0/1 swing traverses the field-induced transition and charge per volt rises ~3-4x; with no remanence the film relaxes back each cycle, avoiding wake-up and imprint.
why: Effective k ~100-150 (fact 1) so the capacitor can be ~3x shorter; hysteresis loss and transition fatigue are the risks.

title: Percolation-edge metal-nanoisland dielectric with giant effective permittivity
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: disperse 1-2-nm Ru or TiN nanoislands in ZrO2 just below the percolation threshold, using ALD nucleation-delay cycles, so percolative/Maxwell-Wagner effects push effective k toward 150-1,000 while isolated islands leave no continuous leakage path.
why: Fact 1: even k~150 would let pillar AR drop to ~25:1; hopping leakage and ns-scale frequency dispersion are the risks.

title: Avalanche-gain readout lets a 50-electron node hold a bit
idea: Scarcity rule: storage charge is cut 300x. Each storage node sits on a junction biased just below breakdown, and during read a stored packet of ~50 electrons triggers a quenched SPAD-style avalanche with ~1e5 charge gain while an empty node stays silent, so a 0.01 fF planar node suffices.
why: Deletes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) entirely with fJ-scale reads; dark counts and afterpulsing set the raw BER that ECC must absorb.

title: Ice sculpture: frozen ionomer double layer locks the gate charge
idea: Stimulus 'ice sculpture' (shape fixed while frozen) -> gate a gain-cell transistor with a nanodot of high-Tg sodium polystyrene-sulfonate ionomer instead of the usual TFSI/PF6/BF4 fluorinated ionic liquids; an embedded nanoheater softens it for ~20 ns while the gate field forms an electric double layer, then cooling freezes the ions, shifting threshold by >1 V.
why: Retention set by frozen ions rather than junction leakage (fact 3); large Vt signal allows tiny cells without a capacitor (fact 1); avoids every fluorinated electrolyte salt.

title: Anodized-aluminum pore template capacitors with domestic hafnium and molybdenum
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD HfZrO in self-organized anodic alumina pores | access: vertical Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C | substrate: U.S.-grown 300 mm Si (Texas) | fab: anodization (no lithography) + U.S.-built ALD tools}. Pores self-order at a pitch set by voltage (~40 nm at ~16 V) and are registered to the transistors by pre-indent dots from a U.S. multibeam e-beam writer; Hf and Zr come from Oregon zircon processing and Mo electrodes from Colorado.
why: Capital/EUV (Fact 4) and U.S. manufacturability: replaces EUV plus high-AR plasma etch for the capacitor layer with a wet electrochemical step at a fraction of the tool cost, and uses no tungsten.

title: Magnetoelectric Cr2O3 antiferromagnet written by voltage, read by Hall
idea: Box = {medium: Neel vector of boron-doped Cr2O3 | access: Si FET | sense: anomalous Hall voltage in an adjacent Pt film | integration: BEOL | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + boron doping to lift the Neel point above 400 K}. Because Cr2O3 is magnetoelectric, its Neel vector flips under a small voltage combined with a static bias field built into the stack, with no charge current through the bit.
why: Energy (Fact 10): aJ-to-fJ write energy, nonvolatile, no current-induced wear, and antiferromagnetic order immune to neighbor disturb.

title: Rare-earth-free Fe16N2 nanomagnet SOT cell from Minnesota iron nitride
idea: Box = {medium: high-anisotropy alpha''-Fe16N2 free layer | access: Si FET | sense: TMR with MgO from Michigan brine | integration: BEOL 3-terminal SOT cell | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputter + low-temperature nitridation from the U.S. Fe16N2 magnet industry}. Fe16N2's high magnetization and anisotropy keep a bit stable at ~15 nm without Pt, Co or rare earths, and spin-orbit-torque writes keep current out of the tunnel barrier for DRAM-class endurance.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: removes Co, Pt, Ir, Ru and rare earths; nonvolatile and refresh-free.

title: Swap single dielectric for negative-capacitance ferroelectric/dielectric series stack
idea: Put a 2-3 nm ferroelectric HZO layer in series with the ZrO2 dielectric, with thicknesses tuned so the ferroelectric's negative-slope region partly cancels the series 1/C term. The stack's capacitance then exceeds the dielectric alone, as transient negative-capacitance experiments showed with 2-3x boosts.
why: Facts 1 and 10 (charge wall, voltage floor): the same charge at ~60% of the voltage, or ~2x Cs in the same pillar.

title: Ephemeral DRAM sized for millisecond data lifetimes
idea: Time-shift the retention spec from 64 ms to the real lifetime of AI activations and KV-cache tiles (often <2 ms between write and last read): build arrays with capacitors 4-5x smaller and short-pillar cells, tagged in the address map as 'ephemeral', and never refresh them; the runtime guarantees consume-before-expire.
why: Capacitor wall and refresh energy: ~4x smaller Cs, no refresh for that tier, roughly 30-40% lower cost per bit for activation memory.

title: Snow globe: electrophoretic nanoparticle position stores the bit
idea: Random stimulus 'snow globe' forced onto memory: a 5 nm charged oxide nanoparticle is sealed in a 30 nm liquid-filled nanocavity between two plates; a +/-1 V write drives it to the top or bottom by electrophoresis, and a coplanar sense electrode reads its position as a capacitance shift. The bit is where a particle sits, not how much charge remains, so junction leakage cannot erase it.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3, ~46 fJ/bit and 10-20% bandwidth) and the high-AR capacitor (fact 1); nothing wears, so endurance is unlimited; claimed ~10x lower idle power if nanoconfined transit is <50 ns.

title: Low-barrier magnetic tunnel junction refreshed like DRAM
idea: Time-shift the magnet's retention from 10 years to ~1 s by designing thermal stability near 25 kT; a small STT pulse writes it and a DRAM-like controller refreshes every few hundred ms, so the bit is held in spin, not charge.
why: Energy and endurance: write current ~5x lower than nonvolatile MRAM, essentially unlimited endurance, and a cell with no capacitor at ~20 F2.

title: Swap solid dielectric for superionic RbAg4I5 electric-double-layer storage node
idea: Fill the storage node with a room-temperature superionic conductor (RbAg4I5, ~0.3 S/cm) against an ion-blocking electrode. The bit is held as a sub-nm Helmholtz double layer (~10-20 uF/cm2), and the high ionic conductivity keeps the RC charging time near ~10 ns at nanoscale.
why: Fact 1: 2-3x charge per area over an EOT-0.5 nm dielectric, multiplied by porous electrode area, so short pillars with AR ~20:1 can be used.

title: Bell-cast parametron: AlN nano-resonator stores bits as oscillation phase
idea: Revive Goto's parametron using a bell-founder's resonator. A shared 2f pump drives an AlN/Si nanobeam, which rings at f in one of two phases (0 or pi), and that phase is the bit. A small seed signal writes it, phase comparison against a reference reads it, and one global pump powers millions of cells.
why: Facts 10 and 3: energy recirculates in a high-Q (~1e4) resonance, escaping the CV2 floor. No leakage tail, and only Al, N and Si.

title: Po: memory made of bubble wrap — micro-plasma ferroelectret void bits
idea: Po: memory made of bubble wrap. Extracted: in a roll-to-roll cellular-polymer (ferroelectret) film each closed micro-void is a bit; a field above the Paschen threshold ignites a ns micro-discharge in the void that deposits +/- charge on its walls (an electret dipole lasting years), and the threshold doubles as the crossbar selector.
why: Packaging-film cost with built-in selection and volumetric stacking (~1 bit/um3, ~125 MB/mm2 for 1 mm thickness) aims 100x+ lower $/GB. Trade-offs: um voids, wall erosion limiting endurance, electrode stacking.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer bit with zero bond-breaking switching
idea: Use rhombohedral-stacked bilayer hBN or MoS2: its out-of-plane polarization flips when one layer slides by a/sqrt(3), so the barrier is only interlayer stacking energy (meV per cell, ~1 eV for a 10 nm domain) and no ion or bond moves. Read the polarization non-destructively through the field it imposes on an adjacent MoS2 channel.
why: Fatigue mechanisms (vacancy migration, domain pinning) need bond rearrangement; removing them targets >1e12 endurance at ~aJ switching energy in an atomically thin cell. Attacks the charge wall (1), destructive read (8) and voltage floor (10).

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN gating a MoS2 channel
idea: Box = {medium: interlayer-sliding polarization of parallel-stacked bilayer hBN | access: MoS2 channel underneath acting as a FeFET | sense: nondestructive channel conductance | integration: BEOL 2D stack on logic | substrate: Si | fab: wafer-scale CVD + transfer}. Polarization flips by an interlayer slip of a fraction of a lattice constant, with no bond breaking or oxygen-vacancy motion, which early reports suggest gives fatigue-free switching past 1e11 cycles at sub-volt fields.
why: Endurance and the voltage floor (Fact 10): sub-volt switching with no ion motion, nonvolatile so no refresh, and an atomically thin storage layer for many-tier stacking.

title: Dipolar molecular rotors in nanogaps store dynamic bits for ingestible pills
idea: Ingestible sensor pills need tiny, low-voltage memory; one mask opens nanogaps where a self-assembled monolayer of dipolar molecular rotors aligns up or down under ~0.3 V, and the collective dipole shifts a sense FET threshold. Thermal relaxation over milliseconds makes it a natural refreshed dynamic bit with no bond-breaking wear.
why: Sub-0.5 V writes (fact 10) and no capacitor wall (fact 1); retention vs density and rotor uniformity are speculative.

title: Colorado River water lawyer: liters-per-gigabit permits for memory cells
idea: A water-rights lawyer prices every acre-foot. Make CHIPS-type grants and state water permits conditional on a certified 'liters of UPW per gigabit' figure for the storage-cell module, with a bonus tier for a 10x reduction, so that dry cell technologies win the funding.
why: Makes US manufacturing viable in water-stressed states (Arizona, Texas, Idaho) and turns the 10x water constraint into market pull for dry storage elements.

title: TOPCon solar contact: tunnel-oxide passivating junction for the storage node
idea: High-efficiency solar cells reach surface recombination velocities <1 cm/s with a 1.5-nm SiO2 tunnel oxide under doped poly-Si (TOPCon); replace the storage-node contact's implanted n+/p junction with this carrier-selective passivating contact plus solar-style hydrogenation, so the node interface has ~100x fewer generation centers.
why: Fact 3: SRH generation at the node junction feeds the 13 fA tail; 10-100x lower interface generation lengthens worst-cell retention ~5-20x, using solar-industry tools that are abundant and U.S.-buildable.

title: Leakage as the keeper: Si/SiGe tunnel-diode latched storage node
idea: Reverse leakage from enemy to holder: two series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes (1990s low-temperature CVD) on a 180 nm cell's storage node cross their negative-resistance curves at two stable points, so tiny diode currents continuously restore '0' or '1' against junction leakage; one access FET reads and writes (tunneling SRAM).
why: Refresh (fact 3): static retention in a ~2-device footprint with pW-scale valley-current standby; no capacitor needed; risk is peak-to-valley ratio uniformity.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric layer amplifies cell capacitance
idea: Scale down to the domain level: insert a thin ferroelectric layer in series with the linear high-k so the ferroelectric operates in its negative-capacitance region, raising total stack capacitance above that of the high-k alone.
why: Capacitor wall: target 1.5-2x Cs without higher AR; hysteresis-free design keeps endurance unlimited.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO layer amplifies cap density in series
idea: Scarcity rule: stay inside today's capacitor footprint, no taller pillar. Add a thin HZO layer in series with the ZrO2, matched so the HZO is stabilized on its negative-capacitance branch; the series stack's capacitance then exceeds ZrO2 alone, raising stored charge 1.5-3x at the same aspect ratio.
why: Raises Cs from ~5 to 8-15 fF without AR 115 (fact 1), or drops AR to ~40:1; must stay non-hysteretic at ns speeds.

title: N: silicon-nitride waveguide loop recirculates bits as light
idea: Hold 64 WDM channels x 100 Gb/s in a ~1.5 m spiral of ultralow-loss Si3N4 waveguide (~10 ns round trip, ~64 kbit per loop), regenerated by an on-chip amplifier every pass, so any bit is reachable from a loop tap within ~5 ns on average.
why: Sits beside co-packaged optical I/O of AI accelerators and avoids electrical data movement (fact 5) with only Si and N and no capacitor; density per mm² is low, so it fits as a bandwidth tier.

title: Eliminate atomic motion: hidden charge-density-wave states as purely electronic bits
idea: Eliminate any motion of atoms or ions: a picosecond electrical pulse switches a nano-patch of 1T-TaS2 from its commensurate insulating state into a metastable 'hidden' metallic CDW domain state; the bit is an electronic ordering pattern with 1e2-1e3 resistance contrast, erased by a longer pulse.
why: ps writes at fJ energies (fact 10) and non-destructive read (fact 8); hidden states are stable only at low temperature today, so the bet is room-temperature stabilization by strain or doping.

title: Charge-density-wave order in 1T-TaS2 holds bits as electron-crystal phase
idea: Effect walk: charge-density-wave ordering. A 10-nm 1T-TaS2 film switches between a commensurate insulating CDW and a metastable metallic 'mosaic' CDW under a ~30-ps few-volt pulse, is read by its 10-100x resistance difference, and is reverted by a longer, weaker pulse.
why: Electronic ordering switches in picoseconds with fJ-class energy and no atomic migration, promising endurance and speed in a BEOL crosspoint; the hidden state is only long-lived at cryogenic temperatures, so room-temperature analogues are needed.

title: Deep-level dopant pocket memory from cryogenic dopant freeze-out
idea: Quantum-computer controllers at 4-40 K watch shallow dopants freeze out and hold their charge state for hours; the room-temperature analog implants, with one mask, a pocket of deep-level dopants (S, Se or Zn in Si, 0.3-0.6 eV) under the access device so captured electrons take milliseconds to minutes to re-emit. Pocket occupancy shifts the device threshold as the stored bit.
why: Capacitorless storage governed by emission-time physics rather than leakage paths (facts 1, 3); one implant mask; capture speed and uniform trap density are the risks.

title: Radar pulse-forming inspired internal-barrier nanolaminate with giant permittivity
idea: Radar pulse-forming networks prize giant-permittivity dielectrics; a nanolaminate of 0.5 nm insulating Al2O3 barriers between 2 nm semiconducting TiO2-x layers shows Maxwell-Wagner giant effective k (~1000), deposited blanket into pillars with one mask protecting periphery. Tuning sublayer conductivity pushes the relaxation frequency above ~1 GHz so the high k survives ns charge sharing.
why: k_eff 10x+ over ZrO2 (fact 1) could cut pillars to AR ~10:1; leakage vs relaxation speed is a fundamental trade, hence speculative.

title: Piezo-strain switched pressure-sensitive phase bit from deep-sea electronics
idea: Deep-sea designers see pressure shift material phases; on chip, a thin piezoelectric (PMN-PT or AlScN) squeezes a pressure-sensitive layer such as SmSe or a Mott oxide by GPa-equivalent stress, switching its resistance 100-1000x, while a ferroelastic latch in the piezo holds the strain. Writing needs ~100-200 mV because strain, not current, does the work.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): write energy ~1 fJ/bit vs tens of fJ, non-volatile and refresh-free; nanoscale strain transfer and fatigue are risks.

title: Bistable photonic-crystal nanocavity holding a bit as trapped light
idea: IFR: a bit that moves at light speed with no resistive loss. Closest achievable: an InP or Si photonic-crystal nanocavity with Kerr or carrier bistability holds high or low intracavity intensity under a shared bias beam (~tens of nW hold), written by fJ pulses and read on a waveguide bus.
why: Fact 5: data-movement energy falls because the bit already lives on the optical interconnect; ps switching.

title: Swap room temperature for 77 K to freeze leakage, planar caps
idea: Run 1T1C cells made on a 28-nm DUV logic process in liquid-nitrogen-immersed memory sleds. At 77 K, junction and GIDL leakage fall by >10^6 and Cu wiring resistance falls ~5x, so a ~1 fF planar MIM cap keeps data for hours and is sensed on short, low-capacitance bitlines.
why: Turns any mature DUV logic fab into a DRAM source with no pillar etch and no EUV (facts 1, 4), and refresh all but disappears (fact 3). LN2 cooling costs ~10 W per watt removed.

title: 77 K immersion pods let storage capacitors shrink tenfold
idea: Jump from cell to datacenter scale: put memory sleds in liquid-nitrogen immersion pods where access-transistor leakage falls by ~6 orders, so retention goes from 64 ms to hours and the capacitor only needs to beat sense-amp offset, not leakage (~0.5 fF instead of 5 fF).
why: Capacitor wall and refresh: 10x smaller Cs, refresh eliminated, enabling short planar or 3D cells; cooling overhead amortized at rack scale.
